title: Projection formula: the pro-étale realization
statement:
Fix the standing finite-field and coefficient setting of [sk-def-sf-setting], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes. At a coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, with finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. At finite coefficients use their pro-etale realizations with bounded constructible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]; at the integral stage use the derived-complete completed-coefficient category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with the finite-level etale-origin witnesses, and at the two field stages use [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The concrete projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection], computed with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$, is an isomorphism:
$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{c}:Rf_!^{c}K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow Rf_!^{c}(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L).
$$
This holds for every such compactification, hence for the chosen realization denoted $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$. At finite coefficients the assertion is in $D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$; at integral coefficients pullback and tensor are completed, and the assertion is in the derived-complete integral category; at field coefficients it is in the rationalized or common-stage category just specified. No discrete constant-$\mathcal O_E$ etale realization is substituted for the completed integral category.

proof.text: The standing setting is [sk-def-sf-setting]. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0,k$, and its spectrum has one point. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y$ are Noetherian. By [sk-thm-nagata-sketch-noetherian], compactifications of $f$ exist. Fix any compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $p$ proper. Since proper includes finite type, the same finite-type/Noetherian lemma gives that $\overline X$ is Noetherian. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to the triangle $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$: $f$ is finite type, $p$ is separated, and $j$ is open, so $j$ is quasi-compact. Write $M=j_!K$. By the displayed definition in [def-exchange-projection], the projection map for this compactification is the ordered composite $Rp_*(\gamma_{K,L})\circ\pi_{p;M,L}$, with $\pi$ the counit-defined proper projection map and $\gamma$ the open-extension tensor comparison followed by $Lj^*Lp^*\simeq Lf^*$. We prove invertibility of this specified composite at each coefficient stage; the integral argument below reduces the entire composite, so it need not prove invertibility of its two factors separately.

source.place: chosen-compactification expansion of the projection transformation; Stacks Tag 01T6 for Noetherianity

proof.text: For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ choose the stipulated bounded constructible etale representatives $K_0,L_0$ and the witness isomorphisms. If witnesses are instead given intrinsically, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies representatives in the bounded constructible etale category. Since $L_0$ is bounded below, [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) reflects the given finite Tor interval of $L$ to $L_0$. Thus the representatives satisfy precisely the hypotheses of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]: the same finite-field datum, the finite ring $A_{E,n}$, separated finite-type $f$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, bounded constructible $K_0,L_0$, and finite Tor amplitude of the second representative $L_0$. The current cited statement requires no Tor bound on $K_0$; no reflection for the first representative is needed. Its pro-etale realization clause asserts the same canonical compact-support projection formula for their witnessed pro-etale realizations. Its final sentence identifies that transformation with the finite constant-coefficient composite of [def-exchange-projection], namely the composite fixed in step 1 for the chosen compactification. Thus this is a statement about the actual map, not just an isomorphism between its endpoints. Apply the witnessed clause and conjugate by the witness isomorphisms; naturality identifies the conjugated map with the component for K,L, and its inverse is the conjugate of the witnessed inverse. This proves the finite-stage assertion. No assertion about completed integral coefficients follows from this finite-coefficient comparison.

source.place: finite-stage transport; finite-etale projection formula and witnessed pro-etale clause

proof.text: For the integral stage work in the completed-coefficient category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and temporarily allow arbitrary $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], both inputs satisfy the uniform finite-level Tor condition: if their first reductions have cohomology in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, their reductions $K_n,L_n$ have Tor amplitude in these same intervals for every $n\geq1$. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](1)--(2), the completed pullback $Lf^*L$ and $H=K\widehat\otimes^L Lf^*L$ are integral bounded constructible. By [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible], the chosen-compactification functor gives $P=Rf_!^cK$ and $T=Rf_!^cH$ in the integral bounded constructible category. Applying the tensor clause of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] again puts $S=P\widehat\otimes^L L$ in that category. Consequently $S,T$ are derived complete. For the later finite coefficient comparisons, [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] puts $Lf_n^*L_n$ in the finite-Tor category with interval $[c,d]$, and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) puts $K_n\otimes^L Lf_n^*L_n$ in that category with interval $[a+c,b+d]$. Thus every input to the compact-support reduction comparisons is in their stated bounded finite-Tor domain. No condensed coefficient category, separatedness of the structure maps to $k$, or site-perfectness of $L$ is assumed.

source.place: Integral continuation of the finite comparison paragraph: explicit completed-operation domains; Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 6.5.4, 6.5.5, 6.5.9(5).

proof.text: Let $u:S\to T$ be the actual integral component $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c$ of [def-exchange-projection], with the completed operations and strict quotient towers of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and the compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. This is the specified counit-defined proper factor followed by the specified open factor, rather than a map chosen by lifting finite components. The integral comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify $S_n=S\otimes^L A_{E,n}$ and $T_n=T\otimes^L A_{E,n}$ with the endpoints of $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}^c$. They identify the map too: tensor-pullback comparisons and the unit and counit defining the transpose of the proper factor are preserved, so its reduction is $\pi_{p;j_!K_n,L_n}$; the open tensor comparison and pullback composition reduce to $\gamma_{K_n,L_n}$. Reduction of their ordered composite is therefore $Rp_{*,n}(\gamma_{K_n,L_n})\circ\pi_{p;j_!K_n,L_n}$. Step 2, applied separately for every $n\geq1$, proves this map invertible. To apply the completion theorem with $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $I=(\varpi_E)$, use [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](2): every ideal of $\mathcal O_E$ is principal and hence finitely generated, so this ring is Noetherian. Derived completeness, with the canonical quotient-tower completion unit and functorial derived-limit model fixed in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], gives a commutative square with horizontal maps $u:S\to T$ and $R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(u_n)$ and vertical completion isomorphisms. The lower map is invertible by [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso]: the strict quotient-tower morphism induced by $u$ gives the morphism of its Roos triangles, and every $u_n$ is invertible. Hence $u$ is invertible by conjugating the lower map by the completion isomorphisms. This is conservativity for a specified morphism between complete objects; it makes no assertion that equal reductions force equality of arbitrary morphisms. It proves the integral formula even for arbitrary integral bounded constructible representatives, which step 5 needs.

source.place: Integral continuation: reduce the actual projection transformation to every finite quotient, then use completeness and the Roos triangles. Agent repair of the finite-only comparison extrapolation; the same concrete reduction argument is written in fix-prop-projection-formula.proof.md, integral reconstruction sentence.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is the raw scalar localization with the same objects as the integral category, so choose arbitrary integral bounded constructible representatives $K_0,L_0$ of $K,L$. The uniform finite-Tor property needed in step 3 follows for these representatives from [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]; no additional lattice hypothesis is imposed. Apply [thm-sf-pf-field] to these integral representatives: its coefficient categories are exactly the raw rationalization and common-stage categories of this item, and its geometric hypotheses require separatedness of f, not of the structure maps of X and Y. Its rational clause gives invertibility of the rational projection transformation. For the particular compactification fixed in step 1, argue directly: apply steps 3--4 to $(K_0,L_0)$ and apply the localization functor to the resulting compactification-relative projection map and its inverse. By functoriality their two composites remain identities. The rationalization compatibility of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] preserves the operation comparisons, tensor associators, units and counits. Substituting these in the two explicit factors of [def-exchange-projection] identifies the localized integral map with the rational component $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c$, rather than merely identifying its endpoints. Thus that component is invertible. This writes the rational continuation directly in the raw coefficient category. The current condensed, separated-scheme theorem det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing is not applied to this raw category: its coefficient and scheme hypotheses do not permit that substitution. The current field-unit realization thm-sf-pf-field supplies this raw-category route, so no condensed-category substitution is needed.

source.place: Field continuation named in the unit paragraph: rationalization of the completed integral formula, written explicitly in the raw scalar-localized coefficient category.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents $K,L$ over finite coefficient fields, and their compositum gives a common finite field $F$. Apply step 5 at $F$. The common-stage clause of [thm-sf-pf-field] states that this finite-stage projection transformation gives the canonical algebraically closed projection map independently of its presentation; its hypotheses hold because both common-stage inputs are represented by integral bounded constructible objects under the same-object rationalization definition. The common-stage scalar-extension compatibility in [lem-fix-operation-reduction], with the morphism convention of [def-exchange-projection], identifies the resulting projection map with the representative of $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{c}$ in the common-stage category. Represent the inverse by the inverse map at $F$. Both composite identities already hold at $F$, so their classes are identities by the displayed Hom-colimit and composition rule in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus the class is invertible, with no construction of an infinite discrete coefficient sheaf and no unproved reflection of isomorphisms by scalar extension. The compactification in step 1 was arbitrary, so all four stages hold for every compactification and hence for the fixed one underlying the notation in the item.
